desc:
Encoding. A singly linked list is passed to your function as an array holding the node values from head to tail; an empty array is an empty list. You may build real nodes from it first, or work on the array directly. The result is also returned as an array of values from head to tail.

Exchange the k-th node from the beginning with the k-th node from the end (both counted from 1). If both refer to the same node, the list does not change. Return the resulting values from head to tail.

For example nums = [1,2,3,4,5] with k = 2 swaps the nodes holding 2 and 4 and gives [1,4,3,2,5]. Try to find both nodes in a single pass without first computing the length.
hints: The k-th node from the end is the node at index n - k (0-based), so you could count the length first. A single pass is possible with two pointers.
Walk a pointer first to the k-th node from the start. Now there are exactly n - k nodes after it.

Start a second pointer second at the head and advance a third pointer from first to the tail while moving second alongside. When the walker reaches the last node, second sits on the k-th node from the end. Swap the two nodes' contents.
editorial: After reaching the k-th node from the start (call it first), there are exactly n - k nodes behind it. A walker that starts at first and runs to the tail makes n - k steps, so a second pointer that starts at the head and moves in lockstep ends on index n - k, which is the k-th node from the end.

Swapping the two nodes is equivalent to swapping their stored values for the purpose of the output, and the pass is O(n) time with O(1) extra space. When k is the middle of an odd-length list both pointers coincide and nothing changes.
